test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 14 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Under Article 164(3) of the Constitution of India, who administers the oath of office to the State Ministers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor of the State**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under Article 164(3) of the Constitution of India, the **Governor of the State administers the oath of office** and secrecy to the State Ministers.
 
• The oath is administered in accordance with the **form prescribed in the Third Schedule** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Governor acts as the **constitutional head of the state** and performs this function as part of their responsibilities.
 
• The oath ceremony typically takes place in the presence of other dignitaries, and the **Chief Minister recommends the names of the ministers** to the Governor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 164 of the Constitution:**

 
 
• It outlines the appointment and tenure of the Chief Minister and other ministers in a state.
 
• The Governor appoints the Chief Minister, and on the advice of the Chief Minister, appoints other ministers.
 
 
 
• **Third Schedule of the Constitution:**
 
 
• It contains the forms of oath or affirmation for various constitutional posts, including ministers.
 
• The oath emphasizes the duty to uphold the Constitution and work without fear or favor.
 
 
 
• **Governor's Role:**
 
 
• The Governor is the **nominal executive head** of the state, while the real executive powers lie with the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.
 
• As per the Constitution, the Governor administers oaths, summons the legislature, and ensures the state government functions within the framework of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Assembly Speaker:**
 
 
• The Speaker presides over the sessions of the legislative assembly but does not administer oaths to ministers.
 
• The Speaker's role is primarily related to legislative procedures, debates, and maintaining order in the house.
 
 
 
• **Separation of Powers:**
 
 
• The Constitution ensures a clear distinction between the roles of the executive, legislature, and judiciary to maintain a balance of power.
 
• The Governor's role as the administrator of oaths is part of the executive function.
